thread.title: Van Wert High School graduates 146 seniors at annual commencement ceremony

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Van Wert High School graduates 146 seniors at annual commencement ceremony
text:
Van Wert High School awarded diplomas to 146 seniors during its 155th annual commencement exercise held on May 27 in the school gym.
The event lasted approximately 70 minutes and included speeches from Class President Grace Spieles and Class Secretary Katie Kramer. Spieles addressed her classmates by saying, “Our class has been described in many ways: involved, determined, and spirited, but I think of one phrase that captures who we are perfectly – anchored in the past, focused on the future. Our memories have shaped us into the people we are today. We will carry with us Friday night football games, spirit weeks, concerts, dances, classroom laughs, and the moments that turned classmates into lifelong friends. We will remember the teachers who challenged us, encouraged us, and believed in us even when we doubted ourselves.” She continued: “These memories remind us of where we came from and the values that brought us here – hard work, resilience, friendship and cougar pride. And although yesterday’s memories may sparkle and gleam, tomorrow is still but a dream, and right here and now you’ve got it made.”
Kramer offered advice to her fellow graduates: “Take all the pictures you can, not to post, but to look back on them and see a life well-lived. Compliment someone if it comes to mind because you have no idea how it could change their day or even their life. Try something new even if it is likely that you will fail; then get back up and keep trying. Make new friends everywhere you go and always treat people with respect and kindness.” She added: “Make sure you set boundaries in life to make sure you are filling your cup—and in turn filling those of others around you. And finally, say yes to every opportunity that comes your way. You never know what you’ll learn or who you’ll meet that will change your life for the better.”
Superintendent Mark Bagley also spoke briefly at the ceremony: “The purpose and endgame of the last 13 years are the life lessons learned along the way through grit and maybe a little failure and success,” he said. “The value of you as a person is not how good you were at these things but were you a good teammate; did you work hard; did you have fun along the journey? You matter.” He concluded his remarks by saying, “Congratulations Van Wert High School seniors—keep on taking care of business—and most importantly don’t stop believing because the best is yet to come.”
Seven students were recognized as graduates of distinction for being in the top ten percent of their class with a cumulative grade point average of at least 3.85 while completing three or more advanced placement courses.
The class selected tulip as its flower; red as its color; and adopted Dr. Seuss’s quote—“You will never know the value of a moment until it becomes a memory”—as its motto.
